title.narrative: Transforming Agricultural Landscapes in Island Ecosystems and Key Biodiversity Areas towards Sustainable Food Systems and Climate Resilient Communities

description.narrative: By restoring 25,920 ha of degraded agricultural land using SLM, ABD and climate-resilient practices, and ensuring sustainable land management over 60,480 ha, the proposed project will directly benefit 110,236 beneficiaries. These people will benefit from enhanced ecosystem goods and services produced by restored sustainably managed upland and lowland, such as access to water, improved soil fertility and quality, and reduced exposure to climate risks. They will be protected against further climate change impacts, like landslides, soil erosion and floods, which are emphasized by intensive monocultural production systems, and land clearing. Increased cash flow can also be expected for the project beneficiary communities. This will be achieved by boosting and diversifying the production of sustainable food crops, with high demand in the sub-region, and by shifting consumption patterns towards sustainable food. Furthermore, additional technical support on agri-businesses (i.e. cooperatives, clusters), improvements in financial literacy and business skills, will improve management at the farm level while facilitating access to financial services that can support investments in sustainable VCs. Additional support for sustainable processing and transformation of agricultural buy-products will ensure added-value of agriproducts from farm businesses. Target support will also be provided to meet the quality and environmental demands on domestic/local markets and increase market access. Business relationships will be fostered by means of market platform and market days, facilitate sales, thereby increasing farmers’ income, which can be reinvested in sustainable agricultural VCs. Increased yields and crop diversification, and improved product quality, which leads to enhanced income, will directly result from the implementation of sustainable land management practices in fields and in the surrounding protected or buffer areas. Positive impacts on agricultural yield quantity and quality will incentivize farmers to sustainably manage their land and reduce any negative environmental externalities.

Improve policy and financial frameworks, production practices and knowledge to catalyze the transformation of rice-based commodity systems from low-productivity and high environmental externalities to a high-performing, integrated sustainable food system generating social, economic and environmental benefits for the Philippines.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.
